title: New changes for hunting programs, what to know about lampreys in Pennsylvania - NewsBreak
text: The middle of August is a unique time for outdoors people. We’re trying to take advantage of what summer has to offer, but we’re also looking forward to the opportunities we have this fall. With students soon going back to school, it’s time to fit in one more road trip to a few state parks and enjoy a swim before the beaches close over Labor Day. At the same time, hunters are focused on purchasing their antlerless deer licenses, Deer Management Program permits and talking with landowners about where they may be allowed to hunt this year. Anglers are enjoying the warming weather and fishing for bass, walleye, catfish and muskies. If you follow social media fishing pages, you’ll see a lot of successful anglers on Lake Erie and the Susquehanna River this time of year. It won’t be long though, that steelhead will be leaving Lake Erie and swimming into the small creeks for spawning. When that happens, anglers from many states and countries will travel to Pennsylvania to catch some of the largest trout our state has to offer. So, use your time wisely this month. Be sure to get out and enjoy another warm month of summer, but also take a few minutes to plan some fishing, hiking and hunting trips this fall. The preparation work you do now, will help you enjoy the experiences that autumn has to offer outdoors people across Pennsylvania. I also have a few stories this week: Have a good weekend. Brian Whipkey is the outdoors columnist for USA TODAY Network sites in Pennsylvania. Contact him with questions about the outdoors or story ideas at bwhipkey@gannett.com or 814-701-6542.
